study_identification_part.si4_title: GPT- based normative models of brain sMRI correlate with dimensional psychopathology

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Evaluate whether GPT-based generative normative models trained on youth sMRI can capture dimensional psychopathology and clinical diagnoses by relating model-derived typicality likelihoods to CBCL symptom scales, ADHD scores, and ASD diagnosis.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states the normative model was trained using a subset of the ABCD dataset comprised of typically developing subjects.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The subjects of ABCD were split into three sets for training ( n= 6,756), validation ( n= 751), and testing ( n= 3,524) purposes. ... our approach is normative as we use only typical subjects (i.e., normal) to train the models.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The sample sizes for training and validation sets are explicitly stated in the supplementary materials. These represent typically developing subjects (lower three quartiles of CBCL) from ABCD dataset.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: "The subjects of ABCD were split into three sets for training (n=6,756), validation (n=751), and testing (n=3,524) purposes." (Supplement L8-L9); "models are normative, trained exclusively with TD subjects" (Supplement L9)
